keyword: how many countries have birthright citizenship
claims: Approximately 30 to 35 countries worldwide offer unconditional, automatic birthright citizenship (jus soli) to children born within their territory, regardless of their parents' nationality, according to recent reports.
About 32 to 33 countries have laws similar to the U.S. that allow unrestricted citizenship by birth.
Most countries with unconditional birthright citizenship are located in the Western Hemisphere.
Most countries in South America have unconditional birthright citizenship.
The vast majority of countries with unconditional birthright citizenship are in the Americas.
Around 50 other countries have limited variations of birthright citizenship.
Most countries in Europe, Asia, and Africa follow jus sanguinis ("right of blood"), where citizenship is passed down through parents' nationality rather than place of birth.
The legality of unconditional birthright citizenship, particularly in the U.S., is a subject of ongoing legal debate.
United States has unconditional birthright citizenship.
Costa Rica has unconditional birthright citizenship.
El Salvador has unconditional birthright citizenship.
